title: A particle pool
description:
Spray particles from a fixed pool, without allocating while the game runs.

```
pool of 256
burst of 50 at (100, 100): 50 alive
after 0.5 s: 50 alive, fading; after 1.2 s: 0 alive
burst of 300: only 256 made, the rest skipped
```
hints: A particle is dead when `life <= 0`; `emit` looks for dead ones and stops when it has made enough or reached the end (lesson 4.03).
A random angle and speed: `float a{angle(m_rng)}; vx = std::cos(a) * speed; vy = std::sin(a) * speed;`.
requirements: A `std::array<Particle, 256>`; each has a position, velocity, life left and colour.
`emit` reuses dead particles; `update(dt)` moves them, applies gravity and reduces life.
Alpha fades with the life left.
stretch: Keep a "next free" index so emitting does not scan the whole array.
